explicitPrefix: Use the installed swift-accessibility-agent skill for this task.

rubric.prompt: Our audit report says: checked 12 elements for missing labels and low contrast; zero findings. It did not test focus order, custom actions, text resizing, or keyboard operation. Can we label the screen fully accessible? Give a short release-note statement that accurately reflects this report.
criteria: Supplies bounded release-note wording without invented tests

rubric.prompt: A patch compiled and a unit test directly called its delete handler with message B. The callback fired once for B. No UI tests or VoiceOver/keyboard interaction were run. Can we conclude that keyboard and VoiceOver users can discover and activate deletion without swiping? Separate what passed from what still needs evidence.
criteria: Does not infer UI wiring/discoverability/input delivery
Requires source linkage and runtime interaction evidence for that broader claim
Does not discard useful scoped result or claim an actual interaction test occurred

rubric.activation: yes, contextual: stale metadata must not feed existing accessible status/description; most assessed logic is ordinary async ownership, so activation is relevant but not evidence of accessibility-specific benefit
rubric.neutrality: Opening states an already-working accessible UI binding and required preservation; it does not identify a reference or reveal generation/currentItem solution. Explicit external replacement and same-item repetition are legitimate product requirements.
essential: Inspect externally managed AVPlayer current item through injected async callback; expose loading/success/error/cancel/no-item state and description for existing binding.
Only active request may accept completion, including same-item repeat; verify actual current item still matches captured item before applying result.
Consume request once so duplicate/conflicting callbacks cannot replace first outcome; cancellation/no-item/new inspection invalidate previous work.
Distinguish loader error from no-item, clear stale description as appropriate, avoid retaining owner through callback.
Preserve player playback preferences and ordinary playback ownership; do not replace externally current item as incidental metadata inspection.
Deterministic synthetic-item tests for external replacement, same-item repeat, cancellation, duplicate, failure, no item and owner lifetime; no network/UI automation.

source_links.claim: manifest media: AVPlayer.currentItem API plus explicitly application request-ownership policy
source_links.evidence: MediaLoadOwner source and nine MediaLoadOwnerTests methods; media-identity/media-duplicate negative receipts

optional: Exact state enum/string names; superseded versus ignored result representation; weak item capture versus safe retained item; item-change observation when correctness at callback application is already guaranteed.

Immediate state refresh at every external replacement, asset-level media metadata/audio description extraction, playback control, actual speech/focus and exact accessible binding implementation are not requested.
alternatives: Inject existing player and inspect()/loadCurrentItem(); token/UUID/request generation plus identity check, with no replace method.
Equivalent observation-driven invalidation plus identity and per-request guard, provided same-item refresh and externally replaced items are covered.
Return state via observable properties or explicit client callback; both can preserve existing binding contract.
missing_fixture_inputs: Existing UI binding/status property signature, loader signature and owner entry method unspecified; answer may define them explicitly. Do not require sample owns-player or replace(_:load:) API.

Task does not specify detecting replace-away-and-back without observing transition; do not add invisible historical replacement or automatic live invalidation requirement beyond active request/current-item validity.

calibration.correct: Owner injects external player, inspect captures current item and fresh token, sets loading before invoking loader; reply weakly captures owner, checks active token and player.currentItem identity, consumes token before setting success/error; nil/cancel invalidate and clear value; tests retain old item during external replacement callback.
calibration.defective: Checks token only: external code replaces current item without new inspection, old callback writes old description. Or checks identity only: two inspections of same item allow old reply to overwrite newer. Or duplicate failure overwrites consumed success.
calibration.alternative: Request object invalidated by new inspection/cancel plus actual identity guard; no owner-controlled replacement API, no integer generation, synthetic AVMutableComposition items and callback array suffice.
calibration.ungradable: Current-item guard or callback consumption hidden in missing helper; absent player injection/identity relationship prevents determining if actual external current item is checked. Inability to execute on current review host is not a subject failure.
